bio:
Joseph Heizler was the herrschaftlicher Jäger, the seigneurial gamekeeper, of the Counts of Kageneck, who were lords of Munzingen, where their Schloss dates from 1672, and from 1702 of Stegen and the Ibental. He was born about 1773 at Weiler, Freiburg, Baden-Württemberg, Germany, and was probably a son of Jakob Heitzler, the Kagenecks' gamekeeper in the Ibental, and Catharina Begelspacher. Jakob's recorded children leave gaps that would fit a son born about 1773, and a gamekeeper's son serving the same lords at their Munzingen seat makes good sense, but the link is not proven. He was not the Ibental schoolteacher Joseph Heitzler (1765–1828), nor the Joseph of the Wehrlehof, and the family records, which give him the dates 1773–1825, may have run two Josephs together.

On 26 December 1799 he married M. Anna Federer of Munzingen there. Their children included Friedrich, born 8 March 1809, Agatha, born 26 June 1813, and Veronica, who died of measles on 29 April 1815 aged about a year and a half. He was therefore alive and living at Munzingen in 1815, and he had died by 7 October 1835, when he was described as the former seigneurial gamekeeper. He is John's 5th great-grandfather.

researchNotes: Joseph Heizler was the 'herrschaftlicher Jäger' — seigneurial gamekeeper of the Counts of Kageneck, lords of Munzingen (Schloss 1672) and from 1702 of Stegen and the Ibental. He married M. Anna Federer of Munzingen there on 26 Dec 1799 (FamilySearch tree event). Children include Friedrich (b. 8 Mar 1809), Agatha (b. 26 Jun 1813) and Veronica (d. 29 Apr 1815 of measles, aged about 1½, 'Tochter des Joseph Heizler'; witness Johann Federer) — so he was alive and living in Munzingen in 1815. He had died by 7 Oct 1835 ('+ Josef Heizler, gewesenen herrschaftlichen Jägers'). The tree gives 1773–1825 and makes him son of Jacob Heitzler and Catharina Begelspacher. Round 1 found no Joseph among Jakob's recorded children (Andreas 1764, Agathe 1771, Franziska 1779, Jakob 1781), but the gaps (1765–70, 1772–78) leave room for a Joseph b. c.1773; a Kageneck gamekeeper's son serving as the Kagenecks' gamekeeper at their Munzingen seat fits well, so the link is Probable (upgraded in round 3). He is not the Ibental teacher Joseph Heitzler (1765–1828) nor the Wehrlehof Joseph — the deep-dive warned the tree may have merged two Josephs. His Munzingen death entry (1815–35) would give his age and perhaps birthplace; the 1816–31 deaths are running text and were not finished.
